messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@redwood.com

Subject: Vendor onboarding: VAT registration, PO routing and evidence needed for Umbrella Logistics BV

Hi Marta,

Thanks for starting the onboarding process — I'm the procurement owner for this account. To get a PO issued and invoices routed correctly we need a short set of tax and entity documents. Can you please provide the items below so Finance can validate VAT treatment and confirm the billing entity?

Required (single reply preferred):
- Signed vendor onboarding form (attached) — please complete section B (billing entity)
- VAT registration certificate for the EU entity (PDF)
- Company extract or registration document
- Bank details for EUR payments (IBAN + BIC)

Optional but helpful:
- VIES confirmation screenshot or link
- Sample invoice showing VAT number and billing entity if available

Notes on PO routing: we typically route POs to the legal entity that issues the invoice. If you operate through a parent company or local branches, please indicate which legal entity should receive the PO and whether invoices will include VAT or be subject to reverse charge.

I've attached the vendor_onboarding_form.pdf to this message (fill and return). Once we have the documents I'll loop in Finance (Irene) and Tax (Ben) to validate and create the PO.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf (application/pdf, 238KB)

Hi Marta — looping in Finance for validation. Quick guidance based on the docs you shared:

1) Billing entity and PO mapping
- Because Umbrella Logistics BV (NL) is the invoicing/legal entity, Redwood will issue POs to that entity: Umbrella Logistics BV (NL), VAT NL123456789B01.
- If you expect some invoices from local branches, please flag which branch and provide the branch VAT/registration — we will consider a PO split by entity to match invoices.

2) VAT treatment
- For B2B cross-border services in the EU, the reverse charge typically applies when we have the supplier VAT ID and confirm you're supplying services to a VAT-registered buyer (Redwood EMEA entity). We'll process invoices under reverse charge where appropriate, but need the VIES screenshot (or an equivalent online lookup result) for the VAT number to maintain tax records.

3) Documents still required for procurement/tax clearance:
- VIES lookup screenshot for NL123456789B01 (vies.ec.europa.eu) — confirms the VAT number is active
- Signed W-8 or equivalent is not required for EU entity but a tax residency letter can help in some countries — optional for now
- Completed po_mapping_template.xlsx (attached) — please confirm which legal entity to bill for which service lines (e.g., freight, storage, customs clearance)

Next steps:
- Marta: confirm that the NL entity will receive POs and complete the attached PO mapping template.
- Logan: once the template is returned and VIES is provided we can create the PO and route to Finance for payment terms review.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Finance Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the docs, Marta — a couple of follow-ups from Tax: 

- Please provide a VIES lookup screenshot (vies.ec.europa.eu) showing NL123456789B01 status, or the VIES query export. This is required for our audit trail. (Attachment: vies_screenshot.png helpful).
- For high-value contracts we request a short tax residency certificate when services cross multiple jurisdictions. If you can provide a one-page statement from local tax authority that would close the loop.
- If Umbrella intends to be paid into a different legal entity than the one invoicing, please do not mix entities on the same invoice. We need invoice-by-entity matching to ledger POs.

Temporary hold: once we receive the VIES confirmation and the completed PO mapping template, Tax will clear the VAT treatment and we can approve PO issuance. If there are any discrepancies we may request an entity split on the PO.

Logan — ensure net payment terms (NET30) are acceptable to the vendor; if they request otherwise let us know and we'll escalate.

Ben Carter
Senior Tax Analyst
